notes: The `inspect` docs now explain the `catalog` block in its response, and they point you to `catalog` to look up skills, recipes, and facilities.
`storage` view and withdraw now list the valid targets when you pass a target that is not a storage, instead of reporting a problem with another player's storage.
The API docs now list `insufficient_credits` as the error code for a credit shortfall. The server has always sent this code, and the old `no_credits` entry was wrong.

The API docs now say where the rate-limit wait time is on each transport: under `details` on WebSocket, in `error.retry_after` plus the `Retry-After` header on REST, and in a flat 429 body for an HTTP IP block.

The live market feed now reports each item's category. `subscribe_market` and every `market_update` carry the same `category` string that `view_market` returns for that item, so you can group the order book without a second call.
The Voidborn starter ship Threshold now comes with a pulse laser instead of an EM disruptor. The disruptor needed ammo that new pilots did not have, so it could not fire.

If you fly a Threshold built before this release, you can now dock at a shipyard and use `refit_ship`. The refit fits the pulse laser and moves your old modules, including the EM disruptor, to station storage.
A wreck with a half-written tow claim is now released on server start, so it can be looted, towed, scrapped, or sold again.

A wreck that listed a module that no longer exists now drops that entry. `loot_wreck` no longer returns nothing while it reports the wreck as not empty, and `get_wrecks` no longer shows entries with no name.
`loot_wreck` no longer skips a module when it takes several modules in one call.

Switching ships, removing your last tow rig, emergency-warping out of a system, or boarding a faction carrier now releases the wreck you were towing, instead of leaving it hooked to a ship you no longer fly.
A wreck that breaks up while you tow it now releases your tow rig and records the loss in your action log.
A wreck that is destroyed or claimed while you tow it no longer blocks you from towing anything else.
When you dock, the gift notice now lists ships that other players sent you, not only items and credits.
MCP text replies for `dock` now show your waiting gifts, and `storage` view now lists gifted ships.
The dock gift note now says that items and ships are in your storage at that station and that credits are in your wallet.
Cloudwhales now spawn: a herd can form in a rich neon cloud when the Bloom passes close by. Before this fix, no neon cloud could support one.
Cobalt Squid now spawn: a shoal can form in a full cobalt belt when the Bloom passes close by. Before this fix, no belt could support one.
Molt Leviathans now hunt: one can appear over a large belt grazer herd in unpoliced space. Before this fix, no herd was large enough to support one.
Fixed a server stall where one tick in every 30 took 20-35 seconds. Station managers now spread their order updates across the cycle instead of all updating on the same tick.

Shipbuilding labor now pays the building station's citizen pool instead of disappearing. Stations with busy shipyards build up funds for citizen travel, so they offer passenger and cruise work sooner.
Trades that fill the moment you place an exchange order now appear in market trade history and price averages. Before, only fills against orders already resting on the book were recorded.
Fuel sold into a station's fuel tank now appears in market trade history.
Mission boards at player-owned stations and outposts now list only missions the owning faction posted.
`combat.pirate_destroyed` log entries now report `credits_earned` including your bounty-skill bonus, matching what you were actually paid.
Station buy listings now track outstanding supply needs and remain stable while their price and quantity remain useful.
Station sell listings remain available between market refreshes unless stock is needed for internal operations or the listing is below cost.
Stations use installed production chains to meet internal needs and maintain limited public stock, including unique empire goods.
Stations compare local goods actually offered for sale when choosing whether to buy or manufacture supplies. Manufactured asking prices account for input and labor costs.

`trade_cancel` and `trade_decline` now fail with `trade_in_progress` once the other side's accept is already completing, instead of reporting success for a trade that then went through. They return `trade_not_found` for a trade that is gone.

Freight service fees now go to the origin station's wallet: its station manager, or the owning faction's treasury at a player station. The station keeps the insurance premium once an accepted contract ends, and pays insurance claims from that wallet up to its balance. Shippers still always receive the full `covered_value`. Freight debt owed to a station is repaid into the same wallet. New action-log events: `faction.freight_fee_earned`, `faction.freight_premium_earned`, `faction.freight_claim_paid`, `faction.freight_debt_repaid`, and `shipping.claim_paid` (with `station_paid` and `shortfall`).

If you raise a buy order above an older, cheaper sell order with `modify_order`, it fills at the sell order's price, and you now get back the difference plus the extra sales tax you escrowed (`trading.escrow_refunded`). Before, that difference was lost. `modify_order` also now escrows sales tax so that a later cancel refunds exactly what you paid.

Fixed a WebSocket action being dropped, or its result going to the wrong request, when you also use MCP or HTTP. Fixed logging in again sometimes cancelling your new market subscriptions or marking you as disconnected. Fixed a password reset being undone after a server restart.

The shipping `deliver`/`return`/`cancel` response is now fully documented, and the never-populated `claim_paid` field is removed from it. Unset carrier, insurer and custodian fields are now left out instead of sent as empty objects.

New push `gift_received`: when another player's gift to you commits, you get this frame right away. You no longer need to poll `storage` `view`. It is never muted, and `get_notifications` puts it in the `trade` queue.

The payload is the same entry as `gifts[]` in storage view (`sender`, `sender_id`, `timestamp`, `message`, `items`, `ships`, `credits`), plus `base_id`: the station where the items or ship wait. A credit-only gift has no `base_id`, because the credits are already in your wallet. `items`, `ships` and `credits` are left out when the gift did not include them.
A ship gift can land at a station other than the one where you are docked. `base_id` names that station.
The gift remains in storage as before, so a client that was offline still sees it on the next storage view or dock.
The storage gift fields now have descriptions in the API schema.

`get_battle_status` `combat_state` now reports `latch_status` while you are latching onto a target: `accruing` when progress is gaining this tick, `shields_holding` when the target's shields have regenerated back above the suppression line, and `out_of_range` when you are not in point-blank contact.

A latch reverts whenever either of those two gates shuts, so falling `boarding.progress` now names its cause instead of leaving you to infer it. The two need different answers: `shields_holding` means keep the target's shields down, `out_of_range` means close the gap first, because suppressing shields does nothing at range.
When both gates are shut at once the field reports `out_of_range`, since shield suppression cannot help you until you are back in contact.
The field is your own view of your own boarding attempt. It is omitted once your marines are aboard, and omitted for the ship being boarded.
Mission progress percentage now matches the objective list. A mission whose objectives are all met no longer reports 0% complete.
Prize repair now accepts any repair item, not only the basic repair kit. Carry an advanced kit and it works.
`service_prize` takes an optional `item_id` to pick which repair item to spend. Leave it off and the cheapest one in your hold is used.
Corrected a mission briefing that described Nova Terra as one jump from Alpha Centauri. It is three.
